items.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I was doing it for Smokey Robinson. I wanted to please Smokey Robinson, because he’s a great writer and producer and artist.

ctx.x: No. The closest I came to that was a female trio from Motown, not the Supremes, and again I’d heard an album they had done and I wanted to do it because I was doing a lot of stuff for Motown then, Smokey Robinson and Berry Gordy and all this kind of stuff. So I wanted to do — I was doing Motown sessions as a producer. And this trio though, on the first song you realized they can’t do it. So I actually recorded them, we did the session

and I wanted to please Smokey, because he was kind of the unofficial head of A&R at Motown when they had — well in Detroit as well as in LA. This is when they were in LA. And I wanted to do it for Barry — I was doing it for Smokey Robinson. I wanted to please Smokey Robinson, because he’s a great writer and producer and artist. And so I brought in ringers out in LA. There was a great background vocal group called the Water Sisters and I used them on lots of records. And that entire album is basically — maybe that…

Do you have a built-in detection system for things that you or other people might want to include on a song, like a really cool part, or let’s put a lute on it or something, and it sounds like a good idea but it’s not relevant to the song.
